name: Batch presentations with Presentations.AI Get Status

parameters.content:
## Start several presentations, then check them later

### How it works
This workflow starts one presentation per topic without waiting, so the batch doesn't hold a single long request. Each presentation gets a request ID. After a 2-minute pause, **Check the presentation status** asks Presentations.AI how each one is doing and downloads the file when it's ready. **Route by status** sends finished presentations to **Collect the file** and failed ones, with their `error`, to **Collect the failures**, so one failure doesn't stop the others. Anything still running goes back to **Wait 2 minutes** and is checked again.

### Setup
1. Install the community node package `@presentations-ai/n8n-nodes-presentations-ai` (tested with version 0.3.2 and later). Follow [n8n's guide to installing verified community nodes](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/verified-install/).
2. Create an API key at [api.presentations.ai](https://api.presentations.ai/#/apikeys) with the **Deck automation** preset, then create a **Presentations.AI API** credential with it and select it on the Presentations.AI node. Presentations.AI charges credits per slide.
3. Click **Execute workflow**. It uses three example topics and creates three presentations, so it uses credits.

### Customization
Replace **List example topics** with your own source, such as a spreadsheet or database, and replace **Collect the file** with an upload to Drive or Slack. The loop stops after about 15 checks (about 30 minutes) through **Stop when it takes too long**, so a presentation that never finishes can't loop forever; change the number in **Route by status**. Replace **Collect the failures** with a notification if you want to hear about them. Add **Slide Count**, **Brand Kit** or **Export Format** under the create node.

## 1. Start the presentations
Create From Topic with **Wait for Completion** off returns right away with `request_id` and status.

## 2. Check until finished
Get Status takes `request_id` and downloads the file when it's complete. COMPLETED goes on and FAILED goes to **Collect the failures** (each item keeps `error`), so one failure doesn't stop the others. Anything else waits and checks again.
